a mobile/online mindfulness program was found to improve quality of life for patients with cancer and increase mindfulness for caregivers, but did not reduce distress or improve sleep.
we demonstrated the feasibility of a randomized controlled trial of an mhealth mindfulness intervention for cancer patient and informal caregiver dyads.

an 8-week mHealth mindfulness program was feasible and acceptable for patients with cancer and their informal caregivers, and preliminary evidence suggests the potential for improved quality of life and increased mindfulness for caregivers.

the development of an innovative mHealth intervention to improve the well-being of cancer patients and their family members.
the use of mHealth mindfulness interventions to help reduce distress, improve QoL, and promote well-being of cancer patients and their family caregivers in an integrated healthcare setting.
the feasibility, efficacy, and acceptability of an mHealth-based mindfulness program to help cancer patients and their family members improve their QoL and reduce distress.

the results of this study suggest that a mindfulness intervention delivered via mobile technology may be feasible and acceptable to patients and their informal cancer caregivers and could improve QoL among cancer patients.

this study demonstrates the feasibility of conducting randomized controlled trial of an mhealth mindfulness intervention for cancer patient and their informal caregivers and the preliminary efficacy of this intervention.
the mHealth mindfulness intervention is a feasible intervention to be tested for efficacy in a fully powered trial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a scalable, cost-effective intervention for patients with cancer and their caregivers to improve QOL.
we were able to demonstrate the feasibility of conducting an mHealth mindfulness randomized controlled trial for cancer patients and informal caregivers.

the study demonstrated the feasibility of delivering an mHealth mindfulness program to patients and their caregivers and that the intervention had preliminary efficacy in improving QoL and increasing mindfulness in patients and caregivers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to conduct an intervention study using mHealth technology to deliver mindfulness training in the context of an integrated health care system.
the use of an mHealth-based mindfulness intervention for cancer is feasible and acceptable for both cancer patients and their primary caregivers.
mHealth interventions can be used to help patients and their caregivers cope with the challenges of cancer.
